name: AK-12
description: The AK-12 is a 5.45mm caliber assault rifle that serves as the standard service weapon for the Russian infantry and is a key component of the Ratnik equipment kit developed by Kalashnikov Concern. Designed for modern warfare, the AK-12 boasts enhanced ergonomics and improved accuracy, making it ideal for extended combat scenarios. Notable upgrades include a length-adjustable buttstock for a personalized fit, an ergonomic grip for better handling, and an updated diopter sight that enhances target acquisition. These refinements ensure the AK-12 delivers superior performance across diverse operational environments.

name: AK-15
description: The AK-15 is a modern 7.62mm assault rifle developed by Kalashnikov Concern as part of the Ratnik program. It enhances the firepower of the classic AK series while preserving its renowned reliability. The AK-15 features advanced ergonomics, including a length-adjustable buttstock, improved hand grip, and upgraded sights, making it adaptable to diverse combat situations.

name: AK-19
description: The AK-19 is a modern assault rifle developed by Kalashnikov Concern, chambered in 5.56x45mm NATO. It's a variant of the AK-12, designed to appeal to international markets that use the 5.56mm round. The AK-19 retains the rugged reliability of the AK platform while incorporating modern features such as a lightweight folding and adjustable buttstock, a new ergonomic pistol grip, and an improved safety selector. The rifle also includes a muzzle brake and a Picatinny rail for mounting optics and accessories, making it versatile for various combat scenarios.

The AK-308 features modern enhancements such as a folding and adjustable buttstock, an ergonomic pistol grip, and an extended Picatinny rail for optics and accessories. It maintains the renowned reliability and durability of the AK series while offering increased firepower and precision suitable for various tactical and military applications.

The AKM, chambered in 7.62x39mm, became the standard rifle for the Soviet Army and was widely adopted by most member states of the Warsaw Pact, ensuring its presence across Eastern Europe and beyond. It was exported and produced in many other countries, making it ubiquitous worldwide.

Chambered for the 5.45x39mm cartridge, it delivers the firepower of the full-size AK-74 in a more compact form. The weapon’s distinctive muzzle brake reduces recoil and muzzle rise. Favored by paratroopers, vehicle crews, and special forces, it strikes a perfect balance between power and maneuverability.

name: Alien
description: The Laugo Arms Alien is a high-performance 9×19mm competition pistol engineered for unmatched control and precision. It features a fixed barrel and gas-delayed blowback system that eliminates the need for a tilting barrel, significantly reducing recoil and muzzle rise. With an ultra-low bore axis (just 1.7 mm above the grip), the barrel aligns closely with the shooter’s hand for superior stability. A non-reciprocating top rail keeps sights or optics fixed during firing, ensuring consistent accuracy. Built on a monolithic aluminum frame with modular internals, the Alien also includes a crisp, competition-tuned trigger.

name: M14
description: The M14 is a 7.62×51mm NATO, gas-operated, magazine-fed battle rifle developed in the United States and adopted in 1959. It features a rotating bolt and selective-fire capability, though most rifles were issued in semi-automatic only. With a 20-round detachable box magazine, the M14 gained a reputation for reliability and long-range effectiveness. It saw extensive use during the early stages of the Vietnam War and remains in limited service today, particularly as a designated marksman rifle.

The M16A1 became the standard-issue rifle for U.S. forces from the late 1960s through the 1970s.

name: M1A

The M1A accepts detachable box magazines, typically 20-round, and is available in various configurations with either wooden or synthetic stocks. Known for its accuracy and robust design, it remains a popular choice for target shooting, hunting, and marksmanship competitions.

description: The MP7A1, introduced in 2003, represents an enhanced iteration of the original MP7 model. Notable design elements include a redesigned pistol grip with a novel surface texture, a retractable stock of reduced length, and side-mounted Picatinny rails for accessory mounting. The folding iron sights have also been streamlined, resulting in a more compact form factor. The MP7A1 is chambered in 4.6×30mm and is designed for maximum firepower in close-quarters combat, offering high armor penetration with low recoil. It has gained recognition for its versatility, compact size, and effectiveness in both military and law enforcement operations.

description: The MP7A2, introduced as the latest evolution of the MP7 series, builds upon the original MP7's design with several significant upgrades. The MP7A2 retains the compact and lightweight profile of its predecessor, chambered in 4.6×30mm, while incorporating a fully adjustable stock for greater stability. The addition of a redesigned handguard allows for improved mounting of accessories, while the upgraded Picatinny rails offer more options for customization.

name: Remington 788
description: The Remington 788 is a bolt-action hunting rifle produced from 1967 to 1983. Despite being marketed as an affordable model, it is valued for its accuracy. Chambered in .222 Remington, the rifle uses a four-round detachable box magazine. It has a distinctive rear-lugged bolt with a short 60° lift for smooth cycling and easy scope use. Its rigid receiver design enhances precision, making it popular among varmint hunters and target shooters.

name: Sa vz. 58
description: The Sa vz. 58 (7,62mm samopal vzor 58) is a 7.62×39mm assault rifle developed in Czechoslovakia in the late 1950s. Despite its visual similarity to the Soviet AK-47, the vz. 58 is a completely independent design, sharing no interchangeable parts with the Kalashnikov. It uses a short-stroke gas piston system, a milled steel receiver, and a distinctive linear hammer-fired mechanism with a hinged bolt locking piece. Compared to the AK-47, it is lighter and features a bolt hold-open device that engages after the final round is fired.

name: SKS
description: The SKS, originating in the Soviet Union, gained global prominence through widespread export and production. Notable for its fixed magazine and foldable bayonet, it lacked select-fire capability and had limited magazine capacity, leading to its replacement by the AK-47 in the Soviet Armed Forces during the 1950s. Despite this, the SKS continued to serve in various Soviet units for years. Soviet production occurred from 1949 to 1958 at the Tula Arsenal and from 1953 to 1954 at the Izhevsk Arsenal, resulting in approximately 2.7 million units. Additionally, millions more were produced under license in China and other Eastern Bloc countries during the Cold War. Its adaptability for guerrilla warfare made it popular among insurgent forces worldwide. Since 1988, the SKS has been widely available in the civilian market in North America, maintaining popularity for hunting and sporting activities.

name: Steyr AUG
description: The Steyr AUG is a pioneering Austrian bullpup assault rifle chambered in 5.56x45mm NATO. Adopted by the Austrian military in 1977, its distinctive bullpup layout combines a full-length barrel with a compact overall profile, while extensive use of polymer keeps the weapon relatively lightweight. The original design also features an integrated optical sight and a quick-change barrel system, contributing to the rifle's versatility and unmistakable appearance.

name: Steyr AUG A3
description: The Steyr AUG A3 is a modernized evolution of the original Austrian bullpup assault rifle, chambered in 5.56x45mm NATO. Building on the AUG's compact polymer design, the A3 introduces extensive Picatinny rail integration for mounting a wider variety of optics and accessories. It retains the platform's interchangeable cold-hammer-forged barrel and compact bullpup layout, while offering greater modularity and adaptability for modern infantry use.

name: SVD Dragunov
description: The Dragunov sniper rifle is a semi-automatic designated marksman rifle chambered in 7.62×54mmR, developed in the Soviet Union between 1957 and 1963. It was chosen as the winning design from a competition involving three design teams. After extensive field testing in various environmental conditions, Dragunov's rifle was officially adopted in July 1963. An initial pre-production batch of 200 rifles was assembled for evaluation, and serial production began in 1964 at Izhmash, later known as Kalashnikov Concern. Since then, the Dragunov has become a standard squad support weapon in numerous countries, including former Warsaw Pact nations.

name: Viper's Colt 1911 Commander
description:
Introduced in 1949, the Colt Commander was developed as a lightweight, compact alternative to the full-size Colt 1911. It was created in response to a U.S. military request for a smaller, more portable sidearm after World War II. The original model featured an aluminum alloy frame, making it lighter than the traditional steel-framed 1911.

This Colt Commander belongs to Aawut “Viper” Phasuk, the leader of the armed group occupying Pha Lang Airfield. Despite his age, Aawut has made a strong mark among Thai soldiers of fortune. He maintains an image of professionalism in every aspect, even in his sense of style. That’s why he avoided any gaudy designs for his gun, opting instead for a tasteful golden touch.

name: Vz. 61 Skorpion
description: The Škorpion vz. 61, also known as the Vz. 61 Skorpion, is a prime example of a compact Czechoslovak submachine gun known for its reliability and versatility. Introduced in the 1960s, it quickly found its place among security forces and military units due to its compact size and firepower. Manufactured by Česká zbrojovka Uherský Brod between 1963 and 1979 under the official designation Samopal vzor 61, the Škorpion vz. 61 features a distinctive design with a folding stock and forward folding grip, making it exceptionally maneuverable in close-quarters combat situations. Chambered in the .32 ACP (7.65mm Browning) caliber, the Škorpion vz. 61 has a cyclic rate of fire of approximately 850 rounds per minute, providing a potent combination of firepower and controllability. Its compact size and lightweight construction make it suitable for various roles, including personal defense, special operations, and as a backup weapon for vehicle crews and pilots.

name: Yen's M700
description:
The Remington M700 is an accurate and reliable bolt-action rifle widely used by hunters, law enforcement agencies, and military snipers around the world. With a reputation for precision, the M700 is available in various calibers and configurations to suit different shooting applications, from long-range target shooting to big game hunting.

This Remington M700 belongs to Bane “Yen” Seeha, the military commander of Midnight Sapphire. Bane is a professional who follows orders and asks no questions. This attitude has earned him a stellar career in the LAF. He does not care for ostentatious adornment and has instead chosen a functional camouflage pattern that suits his work. For him, that is more than enough.
